body:
Closes discussion #575.

## Problem

Adding, deleting, or reordering folios has no undo support today, and the delete confirmation says so explicitly ("this change is irreversible"). None of the existing `QUndoCommand` subclasses in `sources/undocommand/` touch folio/page-level structure — only items within a diagram.

## Change

Three new commands pushed onto the project's existing, already project-scoped undo stack (`Diagram::undoStack()` already just returns `project()->undoStack()`, shared by every diagram in the project):

- **`AddDiagramCommand`** / **`RemoveDiagramCommand`**: `QETProject::addDiagram()`/`detachDiagram()` are the shared attach/detach primitives — list mutation, connect/disconnect of the two per-diagram signals set up at add time, and the `diagramAdded`/`diagramRemoved` emission. Both commands call these (via friend access) for both `redo()` and `undo()`, so a removed diagram is *parked*, not destroyed — it's only actually deleted if the command itself falls out of undo history while still detached (i.e. history limit, or a new action clearing redo history past it).
- **`MoveDiagramCommand`**: wraps a new `ProjectView::setDiagramPosition()`, which performs the tab move and the model's `diagramOrderChanged()` reorder *synchronously* in one step, rather than relying on the queued `tabMoved` connection (needed for interactive drag-and-drop) to catch up on its own timing.

`ProjectView` now reacts to `diagramRemoved` the same way it already reacted to `diagramAdded` (tearing down/rebuilding the tab reactively), so both directions of both commands flow through the same path every other diagram listener (project database, cross-reference items, generic panel tree, `DynamicElementTextItem`) already depends on — no bespoke re-wiring needed per listener.

Multi-folio delete and multi-folio move (`QETDiagramEditor::removeDiagrams()` and the `moveDiagram*(QList<Diagram*>)` batch slots, from the multi-selection work in `0b79dfd14`) wrap their per-diagram loop in `beginMacro()`/`endMacro()`, so a multi-select action is still one undo step.

Also softened the delete confirmation text — it no longer claims the change is irreversible.

## Testing

Built clean (no new warnings). Verified headlessly (Xvfb + xdotool + scrot) against a 7-folio project:
- Add folio → undo → redo
- Delete folio (confirmation text updated) → undo → redo
- Move folio up (context menu) → undo → redo
- Multi-select delete (2 folios) → single undo restores both

One real bug caught and fixed during this testing: an initial implementation of `setDiagramPosition()` used `QTabBar::blockSignals()` to suppress the queued `tabMoved` re-entry, which also silently broke `QTabWidget`'s own internal tab↔page-stack sync (the tab bar reordered but the visible page didn't move). Fixed by temporarily disconnecting only the one app-level `tabMoved` connection instead of blocking all of the tab bar's signals.

Interactive tab drag-and-drop reordering is unchanged and still goes through the original queued `tabMoved` path — not wrapped in an undo command in this PR (not part of the discussion's proposed scope).

Three new QUndoCommand subclasses (AddDiagramCommand, RemoveDiagramCommand,
MoveDiagramCommand) pushed onto the project's existing (already
project-scoped) undo stack, so folio structure edits are undoable
alongside every item-level edit already on that stack.

- QETProject::addDiagram()/detachDiagram() are the shared attach/detach
  primitives: they mutate the diagram list, connect/disconnect the two
  per-diagram signals set up at add time, and emit diagramAdded/
  diagramRemoved. AddDiagramCommand and RemoveDiagramCommand call these
  (via friend access) for both redo and undo, so a removed diagram is
  parked rather than destroyed -- it's only actually deleted if the
  command itself falls out of undo history while still detached.
- ProjectView reacts to diagramRemoved the same way it already reacted to
  diagramAdded (tearing down/rebuilding the tab), so both directions of
  both commands go through the same reactive path every other diagram
  listener (project database, cross-references, generic panel) already
  relies on.
- MoveDiagramCommand wraps a new ProjectView::setDiagramPosition(), which
  performs the tab move and the project's diagramOrderChanged() list
  reorder synchronously in one step, instead of relying on the queued
  tabMoved connection (needed for interactive drag-and-drop) to catch up
  later -- avoiding a second, redundant reorder from that queued call.
- Multi-folio delete and multi-folio move (QETDiagramEditor::removeDiagrams()
  and the moveDiagram*(QList<Diagram*>) batch slots) wrap their per-diagram
  loop in QUndoStack::beginMacro()/endMacro(), so a multi-select action is
  one undo step, matching current UX.
- Softened the delete confirmation's "this change is irreversible" wording
  now that it no longer is.

Verified headlessly (Xvfb + xdotool + scrot): add/undo/redo, delete/undo/
redo (single and multi-select, single undo step for the batch), and
move/undo/redo all behave correctly against a 7-folio project.
